evals.expected_output: A source-grounded design traces HTTP and scheduler creation through exportJobs.create, separates already-committed work from new admission, and evaluates the HTTP-only abstraction against those contracts. The suspension decision belongs at an authoritative creation/admission boundary with an atomic ordering against suspension; equivalent coherent designs are acceptable. Existing resume and worker behavior stays valid for committed jobs. Acceptance evidence covers both entry paths, transaction ordering and absence of quota/job side effects on rejection, not just a route response.
assertions: Traces both postExport and tick to the same creation behavior and explains why an HTTP-only gate cannot establish the stated outcome; an additional adapter check is acceptable only if authoritative enforcement remains outside it.

Places or delegates the new-job suspension decision at a shared responsible boundary and describes an atomic ordering with suspend using the supplied transaction contract, rather than a standalone pre-transaction status read.
Separates new creation from resume/consume so pre-suspension committed jobs remain executable and no extra suspension filter silently changes that contract.

Specifies verification through relevant callers and the creation/transaction boundary, covering rejection without quota reservation or job insertion and a concurrent suspend/create ordering; a status-code-only check is insufficient.

evals.prompt:
Use the local subsystem in the attached files to design a polling-lifecycle correction. Inspect the actual source and callers; do not edit files or produce an implementation plan. You may run node evals/fixtures/progress-lifecycle/inspect-lifecycle.mjs from this skill root for local observations. It uses only fake clocks and controlled promises, not external services.

Product contract: polling exists only while at least one UI subscriber is mounted. Closing one widget must not stop another widget's polling. Closing the last subscriber must prevent new polls; a noncancelable request already in flight is allowed to finish but must not update the cache or notify a later subscription session. Reopening starts a fresh polling session and may display the previously cached snapshot immediately. An offline export remains a pure snapshot read and must never start polling. Within this one-run store, accepted progress must never regress in revision, including when push updates and poll responses arrive out of order. Push transport owns its own lifetime and may still update the cache with no UI mounted.

Give a concise design grounded in the store, both widget callers, and the export caller. State what owns the polling lifetime and stale-response decision, which interfaces or contracts actually need to change, and how to establish that the correction works without mistaking a single-widget happy path for success. Distinguish any observed probe results from planned verification.
evals.expected_output: A design locates subscription lifetime, retained snapshot, monotonic ingestion, and poll-session identity in the shared store rather than individual widgets or the export caller. It traces the two independent widget disposers and snapshot-only export. It identifies both the missing last-subscriber teardown and the need to invalidate old noncancelable poll completions across close/reopen while retaining the revision guard and push independence. It proposes sufficient behavioral evidence using controlled promises and scheduler tokens. If the optional probe is run, reported facts come from its actual output; otherwise no execution is claimed.
assertions: Uses the actual store and callers to distinguish independent subscriptions from snapshot-only access, retaining shared lifetime ownership in the store and not adding polling responsibility to exportProgress.
Accounts for last-unsubscribe cleanup and fresh-session startup without stopping polling when only one of two subscribers leaves; preserves opaque scheduler-token handling.
Explains a stale-poll completion barrier across close/reopen, beyond merely clearing an interval, while allowing noncancelable work to finish without mutating a later session.
Preserves cached snapshots and the existing run/revision ingestion invariant across poll and push ordering, without suppressing push solely because there are no UI listeners.

Defines acceptance evidence for independent widget lifetimes, no-I/O export, out-of-order progress, and an old pending response after reopen; labels probe execution as observed only if it was actually run.

evals.expected_output: A proportionate design keeps range selection in select and UTC day arithmetic with the existing helper, describes the additive through option and mutual-exclusion error while preserving generator timing, identity/order, and old callers. It evaluates rather than automatically adopts RangeEngine. Acceptance distinguishes inclusive calendar-day coverage from a midnight-only or end-of-day precision workaround and checks the unchanged lazy before/since contract. No new module or forced caller migration is necessary absent a justified responsibility change.
assertions: Grounds the responsibility decision in select, the UTC helper, and actual caller usage; does not invent a required RangeEngine or caller migration merely to expand the design.
Defines through as the exclusive start of the following UTC day or an equivalent fully correct inclusive-day boundary, preserving the existing exclusive before and inclusive since semantics.
Accounts for mutual exclusion via InvalidRange and retains generator-time validation/error behavior and lazy consumption instead of eagerly materializing records.

Derives acceptance covering a boundary-day timestamp, next-day exclusion, a calendar transition, old archive/preview behavior, and the both-bounds error, without changing the specified empty-range contract.

evals.expected_output: A proposal-labeled design separates existing external contracts from newly proposed state and orchestration. It derives a per-organization local business-day reminder identity, keeps durable ownership for duplicate prevention across scheduler restarts, and treats timeouts and the finite provider idempotency window as genuine delivery semantics constraints. It identifies the uncloseable read-versus-payment race under the stakeholder interpretation and resolves it by requiring an external coordination capability or an explicitly agreed weaker contract before commitment, rather than asserting that a second read solves it. Verification is matched to the achievable contract rather than fabricated existing code or services.
assertions: Explicitly marks new responsibilities, persistence, or interfaces as proposals and does not invent an existing reminder module, schema, payment fence, or provider receipt-query capability.

Derives organization-local business-day occurrence identity and eligibility from the supplied settings, calendar, ledger, and caller contracts rather than treating scheduler instants or UTC dates as sufficient.

Identifies the payment/read/send atomicity gap and the need to resolve the strict stakeholder contract before commitment; repeated ledger reads alone are not claimed to guarantee no post-payment acceptance.

Addresses durable duplicate ownership across restarts and ambiguous outcomes beyond the 72-hour provider idempotency window, surfacing any unachievable guarantee or needed capability rather than promising exactly-once delivery from a flag.
Ties acceptance evidence and any required pre-commitment contract confirmation to the relevant ledger, scheduler, and provider boundaries, separating prospective checks from unobserved results.

evals.expected_output: A source-based design recognizes that removing the sole blob key and fire-and-forgetting cleanup loses recoverability, while download visibility and physical storage cleanup are separate claims. It proposes durable cleanup intent/tombstone ownership atomically tied to removal from visible metadata, with repeatable deletion processing and a completion rule for idempotent/ambiguous storage outcomes. A transactional outbox, durable tombstone scan, or equivalent coherent approach can satisfy this without prescribing a framework. Existing HTTP and retention callers receive a clear definition of success. Acceptance includes service/read visibility plus storage-boundary evidence after failure and restart, not just 204 and missing metadata, without claiming to prove backup erasure.
assertions: Traces both HTTP and retention callers through remove and distinguishes application download visibility from eventual blob deletion, using the fact that the deleted row holds the only blob key.

Identifies fire-and-forget logging as insufficient for failure/restart recovery and gives durable cleanup intent a clear owner with atomicity against metadata invisibility; equivalent durable designs are accepted.
Defines delete-success, repeated-delete, and cleanup-completion semantics without making application downloads visible again during retries or claiming an unknown timeout proves permanent failure.

Rejects the proposed metadata-only test as sufficient and derives focused evidence for temporary blob failure, restart recovery, idempotent repeated requests, and eventual storage-boundary deletion in addition to immediate new-download rejection.

Matches claimed evidence to its boundary: does not require a real external service merely to test deterministic state transitions, and does not claim a fake or storage API response proves physical erasure or revokes existing signed URLs.
